atoms.b: Traders brought ((++goods goats)) from foreign lands to Egypt, which were sold in ((++markets magpies)).
The Nile allowed Egyptians to ((++transport tremble)) their goods easily on boats to the ports by the sea.
Ancient Egypt didn’t have money, so trade was usually done by bartering. This is a system where items of similar ((++value violet)) are exchanged.

instruction.text: Match together the items of similar value.

feedback.correct: Egypt had access to gold, but not other metals like copper, iron and silver, which were used for tools.
Wood was very useful for making ships, but wasn’t readily available in Egypt.

instruction.text: Select the mode of transport the ancient Egyptians would have used to reach trading partners.

feedback.end: Sailing along the Nile was fast and allowed people to easily transport grain, animals and building materials — including the stones for the pyramids!
People without boats would walk with long lines of camels carrying goods on their backs. This was much slower and they also had to remember the way through the desert!

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Good trade agreements were so important to Egypt that they were willing to go to war over them! Neighbouring countries might have been attacked if they refused to trade.
Trade routes were protected by Egyptian soldiers to keep them under control. Sometimes, important Egyptians working for the government would be sent to live in foreign ports and control trade there.

atoms.a: Which countries were most likely to be attacked by ancient Egypt?
Who would be sent away and given the task of controlling trade in foreign ports?
